# WO-601: Search specs for the people-search brokers (scan searches nothing today)
Status: queued (in-house; vendors offline this week)
Vendor: claude
Agent: broker-researcher (Priya Shah)
Owner contact: Morgan Reyes
Kind: research
Tier: deep
Severity: HIGH
Target release: 0.4
Source: owner real-data test, stage 1 (search only), qa-security 2026-11-11. Private results are kept outside the repo; this WO is PII-free by rule.

## Goal
With the full private registry (428 brokers, 424 enabled) and a real owner profile, `freemyid scan` ran zero searches and `exposure --refresh` loaded zero result pages. Cause: no broker in `brokers/registry.yaml` (or `registry.sample.yaml`) has a `search:` result spec, so `tiers.can_scan()` (`engine/tiers.py:108-117`) is False for every broker and `exposure._read()` (`engine/exposure.py:438-440`) can only end in `no_parser`. Only 22 brokers have `search_url_pattern`; of the 20 enabled ones, 11 are `bot_blocked`, 8 `unknown`, 1 `open` (peoplesearchnow, which now answers a plain fetch with HTTP 403 and a challenge page, though its note says it loaded on 2026-11-07). Result: no CONFIRMED or POSSIBLE listing can ever be produced, so matching, the review step and the "Is this you?" flow are never exercised for real people.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
1. Every enabled broker with `search_url_pattern` has a re-checked `search_access` and `search_url_checked` dated on or after this WO; values that no longer hold are corrected (peoplesearchnow first).
2. For each broker whose access is `open` or `js_required` after re-checking, a `search:` spec (`result_selector` plus the field selectors and `no_results_text` where the site has one) is added and marked verified only after a by-hand check in a normal browser. Bot walls are recorded, never worked around (shared rule 5).
3. Each new spec has a parser test against a SYNTHETIC HTML fixture that copies the page structure with fake people only (Jane Q Testperson, Springfield IL); no saved real result page enters the repo.
4. The public sample registry gets the same specs for the brokers it already lists, so the public build can search at least those sites.
5. A short table in the handoff: broker, access before/after, spec added yes/no, why not.

## Tasks
- [ ] 1. Re-check `search_access` for the 20 enabled search-capable brokers (polite, one request each, honest UA, through NetPolicy).
- [ ] 2. Write `search:` specs for those that can be read without bypassing anything.
- [ ] 3. Synthetic fixtures + parser tests (`engine/htmlsel.py` selectors only).
- [ ] 4. Mirror into the sample registry; `freemyid registry validate` both files.
